bio:
Clark Smith Davenport was born in 1803, by family record at Smith's Clove, now Monroe, in Orange Co., NY. He was a son of Stephen Davenport, born in 1751, and Sarah Smith, and a grandson of Oliver Davenport of the Philipstown Davenports of Putnam Co., NY, which made him a cousin of the Davenports of Plymouth. On 16 October 1825 he married Temperance Pringle of Plymouth, daughter of Samuel and Martha (Lamoreux) Pringle.

The family lived in Plymouth Twp. through the 1830s, 1840s and 1850s and then spent eleven years in Ohio, where they were living in Washington Twp., Wood Co., in 1870; the Ohio years were probably about 1865 to 1875. Their nine children were James (1826), Ziba Samuel (1829–1895), Martha (1830), Sarah Lydia (1831–1918), Samuel Marshall (1834–1920), who married Harriet Gould in 1861, Charles (1836), Lydia (1837–1918), Clark (1840) and William (1843). Clark died in 1875 and was buried in Plymouth.
